# 0 · Getting set up and what you are looking at (12 min)

**R** is a programming language for working with data. **Positron** is the
program we use to *talk to* R — an integrated development environment (IDE).
R does the work; Positron is the workshop it happens in.

## Setup checklist (do once, before class if you can)

> Need bigger, step-by-step instructions? See [**Prep — Getting Set Up**](../../week_0/prep/setup_positron.qmd).

Check each box as you finish it:

  <https://cloud.r-project.org> and install it. Then download Positron from
  <https://positron.posit.co> and install it. (R first — Positron needs to
  find it.)
- [ ] **2. Download today's file.** From the course site, download the

## The panes (6 min)

Positron is divided into **panes**. The numbers in the picture match the
list below — find each one on *your* screen and check it off. Physically
point at it.

![Positron's panes. Your screen will look like this, with your `.qmd` open in the Editor instead of the Welcome page.](images/positron_panes.png){width=100%}

- [ ] **1 · Editor** — the big middle area where this `.qmd` file is open.
  Code you *keep* lives here.
- [ ] **2 · Console** — bottom of the screen, the tab labeled **CONSOLE**.
  R answers here, one command at a time. Code you type here is *not saved*.
- [ ] **3 · Variables** — right side, under the **SESSION** tab. Every object
  you create this session shows up here. (Right now it says *No variables
  have been created* — remember what that looks like.)
- [ ] **4 · Plots** — right side, below Variables. Pictures appear here.
- [ ] **5 · Explorer** — the top icon in the left sidebar (two overlapping
  pages). Click it to see the files in the folder you opened.
- [ ] **6 · Session** — the `R 4.x.x` label in the top-right corner. More on
  this in a moment.
- [ ] **7 · Terminal** — the tab next to Console at the bottom. It is *not*
  R; it talks to your computer's operating system. Know it exists; we will
  not use it today.
- [ ] **Help** — opens on the right side when you ask R for documentation
  (section 3 today).

## The Session (6 min)

R runs inside a **session** — a running copy of R that Positron is talking to.

**How to get to the Session tab.** Look at the **top-right corner** of
Positron (arrow **6** in the picture). It shows which R is running, something
like `R 4.5.1`. That label *is* your session. Click it once: a small menu
opens showing the running R, a **Restart** button, a **Shutdown** button, and
any other interpreters installed on your computer. Close the menu (press
Escape). Now look just below it on the right side: the panel labeled
**SESSION** holds the **Variables** and **Plots** panes — everything the
session is holding in memory, made visible.

Three things to know about the session, today:

1. **It has memory.** Every object you create lives in the session, and shows
   up in Variables.
2. **It can be restarted.** The Restart button (top-right session menu, or the
   Console toolbar) wipes the session's memory clean — Variables empties out.
   Your *files* are untouched.
3. **It can be replaced.** The same menu lets you pick a different R (or
   Python) if more than one is installed. Don't do that today; just know the
   button exists.

Do this now: create nothing yet, look at Variables (empty), and remember what
empty looks like — we'll come back after we've made some objects.

# 1 · Running code and code chunks (12 min)

**LM1 — the Console (2 min).** Click into the Console, type `2 + 2`, press
Enter. R answers. Now press the up-arrow — the Console remembers your last
line. Edit it to `2 + 3` and press Enter.

**LM2 — a code chunk (5 min).** This document is a **Quarto** file: text and
code mixed together. The gray boxes are **code chunks**. A chunk is:

- opened by a line that reads ```` ```{r} ```` (three backticks, then `{r}`)
- closed by a line of three backticks ```` ``` ````
- everything between the two is R code

Look at the chunk below in the Editor. Notice the small **play button** at
its top-right corner. Click it (or put your cursor on a line and press
**Cmd/Ctrl + Enter** to run just that line):

```{r}
# LM2: this line is a COMMENT — R ignores anything after #
2 + 2
3 * 7
10 / 4
```

Two things happened: the results appeared **under the chunk** *and* the same
code ran in the **Console**. A chunk is just a saved bundle of Console lines.

**LM3 — chunk options (2 min).** Lines that start with `#|` at the top of a
chunk are **options** — instructions to Quarto, not R. You will see
`#| eval: false` in this document; it means "show this code, but don't run
it when rendering." Useful for code that is broken on purpose.

```{r}
#| eval: false
# LM3: this chunk is displayed but never runs
this_would_be_an_error
```

# 2 · Objects and assignment (16 min)

**LM4 — the arrow (3 min).** `<-` stores a value under a name. Without it,
R computes and forgets. (Type it fast: `Alt + -` inserts `<-` in Positron.)

```{r}
# LM4: create an object, then call its name
cups <- 3
cups
```

Look at the **Variables pane** — `cups` is there now, with its value.

**LM5 — objects combine (4 min).** Predict before you run: what will `total`
be?

```{r}
# LM5: predict, then run
price <- 4.50
total <- cups * price
total
```

> *Q3. Prediction: ____  · What R said: ____*

**LM6 — overwriting (4 min).** Run this, then check the Variables pane again.

```{r}
# LM6: same name, new value
cups <- 10
total
```

# 3 · Functions, packages, help (20 min)

**LM7 — a function (4 min).** A function is a named action: `name(arguments)`.
`mtcars` is a dataset built into R — 32 cars from 1974. No import needed.
The `$` pulls one column out of it (much more on `$` next week).

```{r}
# LM7: call functions on built-in data
mean(mtcars$mpg)
nrow(mtcars)
```

**LM8 — help (5 min).** Every function has documentation. Run this, and the
Help pane opens:

```{r}
#| eval: false
?mean
```

Read the **Usage** and **Arguments** sections. That's where the answers to
"what does this function want from me?" always live.

**LM9 — packages (5 min).** A **package** is a collection of functions
someone wrote. You **install** once (download to your computer), you **load**
every session (open the toolbox):

```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages("tidyverse")   # ONCE per computer — done in setup
library(tidyverse)              # EVERY session you use it
```

```{r}
# LM9: load it now (already installed)
library(tidyverse)
```

> *Q6. Fill the blanks: install.packages() runs ____ per computer;
> library() runs ____ per session.*
